cover.title: Two pointers
cover.lead: A sorted array and a pair to find: start at both ends and walk inward.
cover.use_it_when: The array is sorted and you need a pair with some property, like a target sum.
cover.why_it_matters: It finds the pair in one walk with no extra memory, where the hash map needed a map.

slides.title: Watch them meet
slides.lead: Find two numbers that add to 10 in 1 3 4 6 8 11.

slides.title: Two ends of a shelf
slides.scene: Two friends stand at the ends of a shelf sorted by price. Too much? The pricey end steps in. Too little? The cheap end steps in.

blocks.text: Each step rules out one end for good, because the array is [[sorted]].

slides.title: One end moves
slides.lead: Sum too big: right moves in. Sum too small: left moves in.

quickcheck.question: Two pointers on 2 7 11 15, target 9. Which positions, counted from 1?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: {{sp(two_sum([2, 7, 11, 15], 9))}}. 2 + 15 is too big, 2 + 11 too, then 2 + 7 = 9.

slides.label: WHY SKIPPING IS SAFE
slides.teaser: The answer, then why it's safe
slides.title: No pair is missed

blocks.label: SUM TOO BIG
blocks.text: 1 + 11 is already too big. 11 plus anything right of 1 is bigger still, so [[11 is out]].
1 + 8 is too small. 1 plus anything left of 8 is smaller still, so 1 is out.

slides.title: Two pointers
slides.explain: Line 8 picks which end moves. LeetCode counts positions from 1, hence the + 1 on line 7.

slides.title: Sorted input only
slides.lead: On unsorted input, moving an end no longer rules anything out.

wrong.note: Every sum is too small. 4 + 6 is never tried.

cost.note: Unsorted input? Sort first, O(n log n), or use the hash map from post 05.

worked.name: LeetCode 167 Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (the LeetCode examples, equal values, negatives, sums at the 32-bit edge) and random sorted arrays of up to 12 values with exactly one pair or none, plus one sorted array of 3,000 large values
blog.tested_against: a brute force that checks every pair
blog.tested_extra: The walk, the check count and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: Two pointers explained with LeetCode 167 Two Sum II: start at both ends of a sorted array and walk inward.
lines: Sum too big: the right end moves in. Too small: the left end moves in.
The trap: on unsorted input like [1, 4, 6, 3] it misses 4 + 6.
